I5.quote: We report on a macroscopic study on the behavior of spillover H atoms using carbon black-supported Pt nanoparticles (CB/Pt) and various organic compounds adsorbed by microporous activated carbon (AC).

notes: The paper studies hydrogen spillover chemistry, but it reports its own volumetric (BELSORP HP, pressure-difference) H2 adsorption/desorption isotherms at 25 °C up to about 3.1 MPa. The clearest carbon-sorbent uptake is pristine commercial activated carbon (MSP20N, Kansai Coke and Chemicals; BET 1980 m2 g-1, Table 1), plotted in Figure 4a in wt% (about 0.26 wt% near 3.1 MPa, read from the figure, reversible physisorption). CB/Pt alone (carbon black-supported Pt) shows no uptake (Figure 1e). Uptakes of the CB/Pt + organic-compound-loaded AC mixtures include irreversible hydrogenation of the adsorbed organics, and the CB/Pt + MoO3 mixtures are not carbon sorbents; neither is needed for eligibility. No statement that the H2 uptake values were published before (ref. 40 is the authors' earlier H2 adsorption work on a different AC hybrid, but the paper does not say these values repeat it). Not a review; record.json is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF.
